properties.decision: One value, `procedural`: a legal, contractual or constitutional procedure between institutions or roles — a presentment-and-veto cycle, an approval chain, a contractual obligation — where the contract is a procedure rather than a protocol or a human-factors touchpoint. Not two values (procedural and contractual), and not an open string with a controlled subset: one word answers the reported case, the enum stays closed so seam checking and boundary pairing keep comparing like with like, and a second governance domain can ask for a second word with its own evidence. Enum values do not move the schema stamp, so this is additive. The ingest mirror (MEDIUM_VALUES) and the tool descriptions carry the same word.
properties.name: DECIDED — Interface.medium gains ONE value, `procedural`, for a rule-governed exchange between institutions or roles
properties.rationale: Reported by the US-government genesis session 2026-08-15: `medium: process` refused, seventeen check-and-balance boundaries filed under `human` and judged defensible by the reporter. Recorded despite being graded LOW because `medium` is READ — library/data earn the single-point-of-failure exemption and seam_report compares it across paired designs — so a procedural boundary labelled `human` is reasoned about as a touchpoint by every computation that reads the field. The first push on this enum (json_rpc) was settled by SPLITTING an Interface rather than adding a value; that reasoning does not transfer here, since seventeen procedures are not one node describing two boundaries. The counter-argument — that the enum reads as software-plus-hardware and a governance domain might want several kinds — is real and is why this adds one word rather than a family: over-designing the vocabulary before a second domain asks is the failure Anthony watches for. Closes fact:the-medium-enum-has-no-word-for-an-institutional-or-legal-contract.
